verses.zh: （大卫的诗，交与伶长。调用百合花。）　神啊，求你救我！因为众水要淹没我。
verses.en: For the music director, according to the tune of “Lilies”;[NOTE:1] by David.Deliver me, O God,for the water has reached my neck.[NOTE:2]
notes: Psalm 69. The psalmist laments his oppressed condition and asks the Lord to deliver him by severely judging his enemies.
Heb “according to lilies.” See the superscription to Ps 45.
verses.commentary:
69:1-4 This strophe is a prayer for deliverance (BDB 446, KB 448, Hiphil
IMPERATIVE) using several images for distress.

- the waters have come up to my soul (cf. Ps. 69:1b; Ps. 32:6)

- sink in deep mire (cf. Ps. 40:2)

- no foothold (BDB 765, only here in the OT, similar to imagery in Ps. 40:2)

He repeats this prayer in Ps. 69:14-15. The ancient Israelites lived in semi-arid lands and were
afraid of water. Even Solomon manned his fleet with Phoenicians, not Israelites. Palestine is notorious for its
dangerous flash floods in the rainy season.

69:1 "Save me" This VERB (BDB 446, KB 448, Hiphil IMPERATIVE)
means physical deliverance.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION (OT)

▣ "life" This is literally nephesh (BDB 659). Here, it may denote
"neck" (KB 712), but if so, this is rare (see possibly Jonah 2:5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

verses.zh: 我陷在深淤泥中，没有立脚之地；我到了深水中，大水漫过我身。
verses.en: I sink into the deep mirewhere there is no solid ground;[NOTE:1] I am in[NOTE:2] deep water,and the current overpowers me.
notes: The Hebrew term נֶפֶשׁ (nefesh) here refers to the psalmist’s throat or neck. The psalmist compares himself to a helpless, drowning man.
Heb “and there is no place to stand.”
verses.commentary:
69:2-3 The fluidity of imagery can be seen in the contrast between too much water in Ps. 69:2
and a parched throat in Ps. 69:3 (BDB 359, the word is found only here in OT, cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 2,
p. 295). Water is a powerful image.

- waters of creation

- flood

- necessary annual rain

- tears

- necessity for life and health

SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS

verses.zh: 我因呼求困乏，喉咙发干；我因等候　神，眼睛失明。
verses.en: I am exhausted from shouting for help.My throat is sore;[NOTE:1] my eyes grow tired from looking for my God.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “have entered.”
Or perhaps “raw”; Heb “burned; inflamed.”
verses.commentary:
69:3-4 Psalm 69:3 is figurative language describing sadness and weeping over the situation
the psalmist finds himself in (cf. Ps. 69:10-11). That situation is described in Ps. 69:4.

- many people (i.e., his people) hate him without cause (cf. John 15:25)

- they want to destroy/kill him

- they are powerful people (cf. Ps. 69:12)

The psalmist asserts that their hatred and attacks are without cause (cf. Ps. 69:4c). He
uses this as a way to denote his innocence in all areas related to the Mosaic covenant. He is not
claiming sinlessness (cf. Ps. 69:5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BLAMELESS,
INNOCENT, GUILTLESS, WITHOUT REPROACH

verses.zh: 无故恨我的，比我头发还多；无理与我为仇、要把我剪除的，甚为强盛。我没有抢夺的，要叫我偿还。
verses.en: Those who hate me without cause are more numerous than the hairs of my head.Those who want to destroy me, my enemies for no reason,[NOTE:1] outnumber me.[NOTE:2] They make me repay what I did not steal.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “my eyes fail from waiting for my God.” The psalmist has intently kept his eyes open, looking for God to intervene, but now his eyes are watery and bloodshot, impairing his vision.
Heb “[with] a lie.” The Hebrew noun שֶׁקֶר (sheqer, “lie”) is used here as an adverb, “falsely, wrongfully” (see Pss 35:19; 38:19).
The Hebrew verb עָצַם (ʿatsam) can sometimes mean “are strong,” but here it probably focuses on numerical superiority; note the parallel verb רָבַב (ravav, “be many”).

verses.zh: 神啊，我的愚昧，你原知道；我的罪愆不能隐瞒。
verses.en: O God, you are aware of my foolish sins;[NOTE:1] my guilt is not hidden from you.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “that which I did not steal, then I restore.” Apparently אָז (ʾaz, “then”) is used here to emphasize the verb that follows.sn They make me repay what I did not steal. The psalmist’s enemies falsely accuse him and hold him accountable for alleged crimes he did not even commit.
Heb “you know my foolishness.”
verses.commentary:
69:5-12 This strophe describes the situation of all believers. We know we are sinful (Ps. 69:5;
Rom. 3:10-18 is a series of OT texts), but we seek to live godly lives (cf. Ps. 69:9a). In light of this tension
the psalmist has several requests.

- may those who wait (i.e., trust) in You not be ashamed because of me

- may those who seek You not be dishonored because of me

This psalmist is boldly asserting that his problems are caused by his faith in YHWH
(cf. Ps. 69:7,9). It is this aspect of the Psalm (Ps. 69:9) that made it a perfect allusion for Jesus
(cf. John 2:17). Also note that Paul, in Rom. 15:3, adds the substitutionary aspect (cf. Isaiah 53;
Mark 10:45; 2 Cor. 5:21) from Ps. 69:9b to Jesus.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHAME

69:5 "my wrongs are not hidden from You" See note at Ps. 44:21.

verses.zh: 万军的主―耶和华啊，求你叫那等候你的，不要因我蒙羞！以色列的　神啊，求你叫那寻求你的，不要因我受辱！
verses.en: Let none who rely on you be disgraced because of me,O Sovereign Lord of Heaven’s Armies.[NOTE:1] Let none who seek you be ashamed because of me,O God of Israel.
notes: The psalmist is the first to admit that he is not perfect. But even so, he is innocent of the allegations which his enemies bring against him (v. 5b). God, who is aware of his foolish sins and guilt, can testify to the truth of his claim.
verses.commentary:
69:6 "May. . ." This is the first in a series of IMPERFECTS used in
a JUSSIVE sense. This Psalm has many of these.

- may. . .not be ashamed, Ps. 69:6 – BDB 101, KB 116, Qal IMPERFECT

- may. . .not be dishonored, Ps. 69:6 – BDB 483, KB 480, Niphal IMPERFECT

- may. . .not overflow me, Ps. 69:15 – BDB 1009, KB 1474, Qal IMPERFECT

- may. . .not swallow me up, Ps. 69:15 – BDB 118, KB 134, Qal IMPERFECT

- may. . .not shut its mouth on me, Ps. 69:15 – BDB 32, KB 37, Qal IMPERFECT

- may. . .their table. . .become a snare, Ps. 69:22a – BDB 224, KB 243, Qal
JUSSIVE

- may it become a trap, Ps. 69:22b – assumed from #6

- may their eyes grow dim so that they cannot see, Ps. 69:23 – BDB 364, KB 361, Qal
IMPERFECT

- may Your burning anger overtake them, Ps. 69:24 – BDB 673, KB 727, Hiphil
IMPERFECT

- may their camp be desolate, Ps. 69:25 – BDB 224, KB 243, Qal
JUSSIVE

- may none dwell in their tents, Ps. 69:25, – same as #10

- may they not come into Your righteousness, Ps. 69:27 – BDB 97, KB 112, Qal
IMPERFECT; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

- may they be blotted out of the book of life, Ps. 69:28 – BDB 562, KB567, Niphal
IMPERFECT; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TWO BOOKS OF GOD

- may they not be recorded with the righteous, Ps. 69:28 – BDB 507, KB 503, Niphal
IMPERFECT

- may Your salvation set me securely on high, Ps. 69:29 – BDB 960, KB 1305, Piel
IMPERFECT (used in a positive sense); see

SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION (OT)

- let heaven and earth praise Him, Ps. 69:34 – BDB 237, KB 248, Piel
IMPERFECT (used in a positive sense)

All of these (except #15 and 16) express the psalmist's prayers for God to act against
his enemies. This is the element of the Psalm that is absent from Jesus' use of this Psalm from the
cross.

69:9b This line of poetry is applied to the reaction of the Jewish leaders, especially the Sadducees
when Jesus cleansed the temple in John's gospel (cf. John 2:17).

verses.zh: 因我为你的缘故受了辱骂，满面羞愧。
verses.en: For I suffer[NOTE:1] humiliation for your sake[NOTE:2] and am thoroughly disgraced.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “O Lord Yahweh of hosts.” Both titles draw attention to God’s sovereign position.
Heb “carry, bear.”
Heb “on account of you.”

verses.zh: 我的弟兄看我为外路人；我的同胞看我为外邦人。
verses.en: My own brothers treat me like a stranger;they act as if I were a foreigner.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and shame covers my face.”

verses.zh: 因我为你的殿心里焦急，如同火烧，并且辱骂你人的辱骂都落在我身上。
verses.en: Certainly[NOTE:1] zeal for[NOTE:2] your house[NOTE:3] consumes me;I endure the insults of those who insult you.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “and I am estranged to my brothers, and a foreigner to the sons of my mother.”
Or “for.” This verse explains that the psalmist’s suffering is due to his allegiance to God.
Or “devotion to.”
God’s house, the temple, here represents by metonymy God himself.

verses.zh: 我哭泣，以禁食刻苦我心；这倒算为我的羞辱。
verses.en: I weep and refrain from eating food,[NOTE:1] which causes others to insult me.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the insults of those who insult you fall upon me.”sn Jn 2:17 applies the first half of this verse to Jesus’ ministry in the context of John’s account of Jesus cleansing the temple.
Fasting was a practice of mourners. By refraining from normal activities such as eating food, the mourner demonstrated the sincerity of his sorrow.
verses.commentary:
69:10-11 The psalmist's very acts of prayer and humility became "a reproach" (BDB 357),
"a byword" (BDB 605) to his powerful friends (i.e., "those who sit in the gate,"
Ps. 69:12a), as well as the drunkards (Ps. 69:12b).

▣ "fasting. . .sackcloth" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING
RITES and
SPECIAL TOPIC: FASTING.

Notice the contrast between the people of verses 5-12.

- the pious writer who serves God in prayer, fasting, and service

- the impious at the gate (i.e., place of leadership) who belittle his devotion and make up
drunken songs

verses.zh: 我拿麻布当衣裳，就成了他们的笑谈。
verses.en: I wear sackclothand they ridicule me.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and it becomes insults to me.”

verses.zh: 坐在城门口的谈论我；酒徒也以我为歌曲。
verses.en: Those who sit at the city gate gossip about me;drunkards mock me in their songs.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and I am an object of ridicule to them.”
verses.commentary:
69:12 "Those who sit in the gate" This is a standard idiom for the leaders of a city (cf. Gen. 19:1; Ruth 4:1).
The gate was a place of

- fellowship

- purchasing

- judgment (i.e., city council)

This verse describes the abuse the psalmist experienced from two diverse groups.

- leaders at the gate

- drunkards in the streets

verses.zh: 但我在悦纳的时候向你―耶和华祈祷。　神啊，求你按你丰盛的慈爱，凭你拯救的诚实应允我！
verses.en: O Lord, may you hear my prayer and be favorably disposed to me.[NOTE:1] O God, because of your great loyal love, answer me with your faithful deliverance.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the mocking songs of the drinkers of beer.”
Heb “as for me, [may] my prayer be to you, O Lord, [in] a time of favor.”
verses.commentary:
69:13-15 The psalmist continues his prayers. They are expressed

- to YHWH

- at an acceptable time

Notice the psalmist's trust in YHWH even amidst his troubled times and knowledge that
at the appropriate time He will answer and save (cf. Ps. 32:6; Isa. 49:8; 2 Cor. 6:2). There is an
appropriate time (cf. Eccl. 3:1-8).

The psalmist trusts in YHWH's

- lovingkindness (see
SPECIAL
TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS [hesed]), Ps. 69:13b

- faithfulness (see
SPECIAL
TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS IN THE OT), Ps. 69:13c

Notice the two IMPERATIVES.

- answer me – BDB 722, KB 851, Qal IMPERATIVES, Ps. 69:13c

- deliver me – BDB 664, KB 717, Hiphil IMPERATIVE, Ps. 69:14a

Psalm 69:14-15 describes what the psalmist seeks to be delivered from.

- do not let me sink (cf. Ps. 69:1-2). There is a different parsing in

- Analytical Key to the OT, by John Owens, where it is identified as a Qal
IMPERATIVE (p. 374)

- OT Parsing Guide, by Beall, Banks and Smith, identifies it as a Qal
COHORTATIVE (p. 439)

- may I be delivered from. . . There is a different parsing in

- Analytical Key – Niphal IMPERFECT (p. 374)

- Parsing Guide – Niphal COHORTATIVE (p. 439)

The psalmist describes his adversaries as "his foes" and "deep places of
water" (Ps. 69:14b). Psalm 69:14 and 15 use the same imagery as Ps. 69:1-2 (cf. Ps. 124:4-5; Isa. 43:2).

69:15c "the pit" This is imagery for Sheol, the holding place of the dead, which is
often parallel to "the pit" (cf. Num. 16:33; Ps. 28:1; 88:3-4; Prov. 1:12). It could refer to the grave (cf. Ps. 141:7).

SPECIAL
TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?, I. B.

verses.zh: 求你搭救我出离淤泥，不叫我陷在其中；求你使我脱离那些恨我的人，使我出离深水。
verses.en: Rescue me from the mud. Don’t let me sink.Deliver me[NOTE:1] from those who hate me,from the deep water.
notes: Heb “O God, in the abundance of your loyal love, answer me in the faithfulness of your deliverance.”

verses.zh: 求你不容大水漫过我，不容深渊吞灭我，不容坑坎在我以上合口。
verses.en: Don’t let the current overpower me.Don’t let the deep swallow me up.Don’t let the Pit[NOTE:1] devour me.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “let me be delivered.”
Heb “well,” which here symbolizes the place of the dead (cf. Ps 55:23).

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你应允我！因为你的慈爱本为美好；求你按你丰盛的慈悲回转眷顾我！
verses.en: Answer me, O Lord, for your loyal love is good.[NOTE:1] Because of your great compassion, turn toward me.
notes: Heb “do not let the well close its mouth upon me.”
verses.commentary:
69:16-19 This strophe is characterized by IMPERATIVES OF ENTREATY.

- answer me, Ps. 69:16 – BDB 772 I, KB 851, Qal IMPERATIVE

- turn to me, Ps. 69:16 – BDB 815, KB 937, Qal IMPERATIVE
(cf. Ps. 27:9; 102:2; 143:7)

- quickly (lit. hasten), Ps. 69:17 – BDB 554, KB 553, Piel IMPERATIVE

- answer me, Ps. 69:17 – same as #1

- draw near to me, Ps. 69:18 – BDB 897, KB 1132, Qal IMPERATIVE

- redeem me, Ps. 69:18 – BDB 145 I, KB 165, Qal IMPERATIVE

- ransom me, Ps. 69:18 – BDB 804, KB 911, Qal IMPERATIVE (see
SPECIAL
TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM)

Notice the basis for these prayer requests is:

- YHWH's lovingkindness (BDB 338) is good, Ps. 69:16

- YHWH's great compassion (lit. "mercies," BDB 933), Ps. 69:16

- YHWH knows the psalmist's situation, Ps. 69:19

- the psalmist's heart

- the adversaries' hearts

SPECIAL
TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS (hesed)

verses.zh: 不要掩面不顾你的仆人；我是在急难之中，求你速速地应允我！
verses.en: Do not ignore[NOTE:1] your servant,for I am in trouble. Answer me right away.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “pleasant”; or “desirable.”
Heb “do not hide your face from.” The Hebrew idiom “hide the face” can (1) mean “ignore” (see Pss 10:11; 13:1; 51:9) or (2) carry the stronger idea of “reject” (see Pss 30:7; 88:14).
verses.commentary:
69:17 "do not hide your face" This anthropomorphic phrase is imagery for

- YHWH's personal notice and attention

- based on Aaronic blessing of Num. 6:24-26

- Sin causes a break in the fellowship with YHWH. The psalmist has admitted his sin, v. 5.

- The psalmist is trusting in YHWH's unchanging character of mercy and covenant loyalty.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE GOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

▣ "Your servant" This could mean

- a special leader, like Moses, Joshua

- a reference to David or his royal descendants (i.e., ultimately the Messiah)

- the special Servant of the Messianic poems of Isaiah 40-55

- just a title for a covenant believer (cf. Ps. 69:36)

SPECIAL TOPIC: MY SERVANT

verses.zh: 求你亲近我，救赎我！求你因我的仇敌把我赎回！
verses.en: Come near me and redeem me.[NOTE:1] Because of my enemies, rescue me.
notes: Or “quickly.”
verses.commentary:
69:18 "redeem" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

verses.zh: 你知道我受的辱骂、欺凌、羞辱；我的敌人都在你面前。
verses.en: You know how I am insulted, humiliated, and disgraced;you can see all my enemies.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “come near my life and redeem it.” The verb “redeem” casts the Lord in the role of a leader who protects members of his extended family in times of need and crisis (see Ps 19:14).
verses.commentary:
69:19 Most English translations see Ps. 69:19 as going with Ps. 69:20-21.

Notice the eastern view of life that emphasizes one's reputation.

- reproach – BDB 357, cf. Ps. 69:20

- shame – BDB 102

- dishonor – BDB 484

verses.zh: 辱骂伤破了我的心，我又满了忧愁。我指望有人体恤，却没有一个；我指望有人安慰，却找不着一个。
verses.en: Their insults are painful[NOTE:1] and make me lose heart;[NOTE:2] I look[NOTE:3] for sympathy, but receive none,[NOTE:4] for comforters, but find none.
notes: Heb “before you [are] all my enemies.”
Heb “break my heart.” The “heart” is viewed here as the origin of the psalmist’s emotions.

The verb form appears to be a Qal preterite from an otherwise unattested root נוּשׁ (nush), which some consider an alternate form of אָנַשׁ (ʾanash, “be weak; be sick”; see BDB 60 s.v. I אָנַשׁ). Perhaps the form should be emended to a Niphal, וָאֵאָנְשָׁה (vaʾeʾaneshah, “and I am sick”). The Niphal of אָנַשׁ occurs in 2 Sam 12:15, where it is used to describe David’s sick child.
Heb “wait.”
verses.commentary:
69:20

NASB, NKJV, JPSOA, LXX, Peshitta
"Reproach"

NRSV, NJB, REB, TEV
"insults"

This Hebrew FEMININE NOUN (BDB 357, KB 356) is used of taunting
by enemies, cf. Ps. 22:7. This same root is used in Ps. 71:13; 89:51; 119:22; Prov. 18:3.

▣ "heart" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

▣ "I am so sick" This VERB (BDB 633, KB 683) is found only here
in the OT.

- The BDB suggests "sick" (BDB 60)

- KB suggests "incurable"

- NJB has "passed cure"

- Possibly it means "in despair" (cf. NRSV, TEV, JPSOA)

If "sick," then Ps. 69:29 is a parallel.

▣ "for comforters" This PARTICIPLE (BDB 636, KB 688, Piel ACTIVE) is
used of Job's "comforters" in Job 16:2; 21:34,

verses.zh: 他们拿苦胆给我当食物；我渴了，他们拿醋给我喝。
verses.en: They put bitter poison[NOTE:1] into my food,and to quench my thirst they give me vinegar to drink.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and I wait for sympathy, but there is none.” The form נוּד (nud) is an infinitive functioning as a verbal noun:, “sympathizing.” Some suggest emending the form to a participle נָד (nad, “one who shows sympathy”). The verb נוּד (nud) also has the nuance “show sympathy” in Job 2:11; 42:11 and Isa 51:19.
According to BDB 912 s.v. II רֹאשׁ the term can mean “a bitter and poisonous plant.”
verses.commentary:
69:21 The Hebrew word for "gall" (Ps. 69:21) is "poison" (BDB 912 II), but
can refer to bad wine (cf. Deut. 32:32). It is the LXX that changed it to "gall" or
"bile" (green – cholē). In context this "poison" and
"vinegar" refer to the insults of the psalmist's antagonists (i.e., covenant partners, close
friends, and family, cf. Ps. 69:8).

This strophe is quoted in Matt. 27:34 as being fulfilled in Jesus' crucifixion. Psalm 69:21b
is alluded to in Mark 15:23; Luke 23:36; John 19:28-30. This Psalm and Psalm 22 are the two OT allusions
and quotes that the NT uses of Jesus' crucifixion experience.

These Psalms are not predictive but typological. See notes at Psalm 22. Psalm 69:22-28
does not fit Jesus' attitudes or words from the cross.

SPECIAL TOPIC: TYPOLOGY

69:21 "vinegar" This term (BDB 330) refers to a cheap wine (cf. Num. 6:3). See
SPECIAL TOPIC: ALCOHOL AND
ALCOHOLISM.

verses.zh: 愿他们的筵席在他们面前变为网罗，在他们平安的时候变为机槛。
verses.en: May their dining table become a trap before them.May it be a snare for that group of friends.[NOTE:1]
notes: John 19:28-30 appears to understand Jesus’ experience on the cross as a fulfillment of this passage (or Ps 22:15). See the study note on the word “thirsty” in John 19:28.
verses.commentary:
69:22-28 This strophe discusses what the psalmist requests that YHWH will do to his enemies. See
notes at Ps. 69:6 (IMPERFECTS used as JUSSIVES). There are

- three JUSSIVES

- five IMPERFECTS used in a JUSSIVE sense

- two IMPERATIVES

- make their loins shake continually – BDB 588, KB 609, Hiphil
IMPERATIVE (this is the poetic opposite of Ps. 69:29b)

- pour out Your indignation on them – BDB 1049, KB 1629, Qal
IMPERATIVE

This strophe is alluded to or quoted several times in the NT.

- Psalm 69:22 is quoted in Rom. 11:9-10, which deals with unbelieving Israel.

- Psalm 69:25 is quoted in Acts 1:20 about the "Field of Blood" purchased by the priests with Judas' betrayal money.

- Psalm 69:27a may be alluded to in Rom. 1:28, which deals with the sinfulness of all humanity (cf. Rom. 3:9-18, 23).

69:22b

NASB
"when they are in peace"

NKJV
"their well-being"

TEV
"sacred feasts"

NJB
"their abundance"

REB
"when they feel secure"

JPSOA
"a snare for their allies"

Peshitta
"that which should have been for their reward, let it be a trap"

LXX
"a retribution and a stumbling block"

The MT has "security" (BDB 1022) but the Aramaic Targums have "sacrificial
feasts" (cf. NRSV, TEV). The NRSV changes it to "a snare for their allies" (cf. JPSOA)
using an idiom from Ps. 55:20 (i.e., close friends).

The problem is the root, שׁלם. It can mean

- be complete, sound ‒ BDB 1022, VERB

- welfare, peace ‒ שׁלום, BDB 1022, NOUN

- sacrifice for allies, peace offering ‒ BDB 1023, NOUN (RSV)

- be in covenant of peace ‒ BDB 1023, VERB

- safe; at peace ‒ BDB 1023, ADJECTIVE

- physical location ‒ BDB 1024, cf. Gen. 14:18; Ps. 76:2 (i.e., city of Salem)

- a proper name ‒ BDB 1024, in the tribal, Gen. 46:24; Num. 26:49

- recompense ‒ BDB 1024, NOUN, cf. Deut. 32:35

The UBS Text Project, p. 301, gives a "C" rating to "and for the secure ones."

verses.zh: 愿他们的眼睛昏蒙，不得看见；愿你使他们的腰常常战抖。
verses.en: May their eyes be blinded.[NOTE:1] Make them shake violently.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and to the friends for a snare.” The plural of שָׁלוֹם (shalom, “peace”) is used in Ps 55:20 of one’s “friends.” If the reading of the MT is retained here, the term depicts the psalmist’s enemies as a close-knit group of friends who are bound together by their hatred for the psalmist. Some prefer to revocalize the text as וּלְשִׁלּוּמִים (uleshillumim, “and for retribution”). In this case the noun stands parallel to פַּח (pakh, “trap”) and מוֹקֵשׁ (moqesh, “snare”), and one might translate, “may their dining table become a trap before them, [a means of] retribution and a snare” (cf. NIV).
Heb “may their eyes be darkened from seeing.”

verses.zh: 求你将你的恼恨倒在他们身上，叫你的烈怒追上他们。
verses.en: Pour out your judgment[NOTE:1] on them.May your raging anger[NOTE:2] overtake them.
notes: Heb “make their hips shake continually.”
Heb “anger.” “Anger” here refers metonymically to divine judgment, which is the practical effect of God’s anger.

verses.zh: 愿他们的住处变为荒场；愿他们的帐棚无人居住。
verses.en: May their camp become desolate,their tents uninhabited.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the rage of your anger.” The phrase “rage of your anger” employs an appositional genitive. Synonyms are joined in a construct relationship to emphasize the single idea. For a detailed discussion of the grammatical point with numerous examples, see Y. Avishur, “Pairs of Synonymous Words in the Construct State (and in Appositional Hendiadys) in Biblical Hebrew,” Semitics 2 (1971), 17-81.
verses.commentary: 69:25 This is imagery from the Wilderness Wandering Period; a common idiom from Israel's past.

verses.zh: 因为，你所击打的，他们就逼迫；你所击伤的，他们戏说他的愁苦。
verses.en: For they harass[NOTE:1] the one whom you discipline;[NOTE:2] they spread the news about the suffering of those whom you punish.[NOTE:3]
notes: In Acts 1:20 Peter applies the language of this verse to Judas’ experience. By changing the pronouns from plural to singular, he is able to apply the ancient curse, pronounced against the psalmist’s enemies, to Judas in particular.tn Heb “in their tents may there not be one who dwells.”
Or “persecute”; Heb “chase.”
Heb “for you, the one whom you strike, they chase.”
verses.commentary:
69:26 This verse seems to reflect Isa. 53:4 and 10 (cf. 2 Cor. 5:21).

The VERB form (BDB 319) of the NOUN translated
"wounded" appears in Isa. 53:5 (BDB 319, KB 320, Poal PARTICIPLE). The
VERB "smitten" (BDB 645, KB 697, Hophal PARTICIPLE) also
occurs in Isa. 53:4.

Psalm 69:21 and 26 surely would have caused the Gospel writers to see a connection!

verses.zh: 愿你在他们的罪上加罪，不容他们在你面前称义。
verses.en: Hold them accountable for all their sins.[NOTE:1] Do not vindicate them.[NOTE:2]
notes: The psalmist is innocent of the false charges made by his enemies (v. 4), but he is also aware of his sinfulness (v. 5) and admits that he experiences divine discipline (v. 26) despite his devotion to God (v. 9). Here he laments that his enemies take advantage of such divine discipline by harassing and slandering him. They “kick him while he’s down,” as the expression goes.tn Heb “they announce the pain of your wounded ones” (i.e., “the ones whom you wounded,” as the parallel line makes clear).
Heb “place sin upon their sin.”

verses.zh: 愿他们从生命册上被涂抹，不得记录在义人之中。
verses.en: May their names be deleted from the scroll of the living.[NOTE:1] Do not let their names be listed with the godly.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “let them not come into your vindication.”

Heb “let them be wiped out of the scroll of the living.”sn The phrase the scroll of the living occurs only here in the OT. It pictures a scroll or census list containing the names of the citizens of a community. When an individual died, that person’s name was removed from the list. So this curse is a very vivid way of asking that the enemies die.
verses.commentary:
69:28 In the ANE names of citizens of a city were recorded on a roll. The Bible uses this imagery
to reflect God's knowledge.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TWO
BOOKS OF GOD

verses.zh: 但我是困苦忧伤的；　神啊，愿你的救恩将我安置在高处。
verses.en: I am oppressed and suffering.O God, deliver and protect me.[NOTE:1]
notes: Do not let their names be listed with the godly. This curse pictures a scroll in which God records the names of his loyal followers. The psalmist makes the point that his enemies have no right to be included in this list of the godly.tn Heb “and with the godly let them not be written.”
verses.commentary:
69:29-33 This strophe describes what the delivered psalmist will do because YHWH's salvation
has set him securely on high.

- I will praise the name of God with song

- I will magnify Him with thanksgiving

This implies a tabernacle/temple setting, as does Ps. 69:31 (a sacrifice). Psalm 69:9 is also an
allusion to the tabernacle/temple (i.e., "Your house" and "consumed as a sacrificial fire").

YHWH's deliverance of the falsely accused and abused psalmist causes others to rejoice
and trust in Him (cf. Ps. 69:32-33).

69:29 "afflicted" From this term (BDB 776) and the rare word in Ps. 69:20, "sick"
or "in despair," many commentators have asserted that the psalmist is ill, but I think the
context denotes persecution and psychological distress, not physical illness, though they are often
connected (i.e., cause and effect).

It is also possible that the imagery of illness is used as another way to affirm the
psalmist's sense of sin (cf. Ps. 69:5). Healing is often an idiom for forgiveness (cf. Ps. 103:3;
Isa. 1:5-6).

verses.zh: 我要以诗歌赞美　神的名，以感谢称他为大！
verses.en: I will sing praises to God’s name.[NOTE:1] I will magnify him as I give him thanks.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “your deliverance, O God, may it protect me.”
Heb “I will praise the name of God with a song.”

verses.zh: 这便叫耶和华喜悦，胜似献牛，或是献有角有蹄的公牛。
verses.en: That will please the Lord more than an ox or a bullwith horns and hooves.
verses.commentary:
69:31 This verse is used theologically by post A.D. 70 Judaism for the substitution
of "praise" for "sacrifice" (cf. Ps. 40:6; 50:13-14; 51:16-17; 141:2). Praise pleases God.

verses.zh: 谦卑的人看见了就喜乐；寻求　神的人，愿你们的心苏醒。
verses.en: The oppressed look on—let them rejoice.You who seek God,[NOTE:1] may you be encouraged.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “I will magnify him with thanks.”
You who seek God refers to those who seek to have a relationship with God by obeying and worshiping him (see Ps 53:2).

verses.zh: 因为耶和华听了穷乏人，不藐视被囚的人。
verses.en: For the Lord listens to the needy;he does not despise his captive people.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “may your heart[s] live.” See Ps 22:26.

verses.zh: 愿天和地、洋海和其中一切的动物都赞美他！
verses.en: Let the heavens and the earth praise him,along with the seas and everything that swims in them.
verses.commentary:
69:34-36 As so often in the Psalm, there is a final small strophe which is used in corporate
worship (i.e., Ps. 103:19-22). The God of creation is also the God of Israel, who dwells in Zion/Judah
with His people. They are characterized as

- the seed of His servants

- those who love His name

If this Psalm were of David's time, it would have "Israel," not "Judah," so
either

- David did not write it (i.e., cannot trust titles of the Psalms; they are absent in the Dead
Sea Scrolls and often do not fit the textual information in the Psalm)

- someone added the last strophe later, possibly after an exile

69:34 "heaven and earth. . .seas" These three NOUNS are used to denote
all of creation (cf. Exod. 20:4,11; Deut. 5:8; Ps. 96:11; 135:6; 146:6; Hag. 2:6).

- earth's atmosphere

- earth's land

- earth's oceans and lakes

verses.zh: 因为　神要拯救锡安，建造犹大的城邑；他的民要在那里居住，得以为业。
verses.en: For God will deliver Zionand rebuild the cities of Judah,and his people[NOTE:1] will again live in them and possess Zion.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “his prisoners he does not despise.”
Heb “they”; the referent (God’s people) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 他仆人的后裔要承受为业；爱他名的人也要住在其中。
verses.en: The descendants of his servants will inherit it,and those who are loyal to him[NOTE:1] will live in it.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “it.” The third feminine singular pronominal suffix probably refers to “Zion” (see Pss 48:12; 102:14); thus the referent has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “the lovers of his name.” The phrase refers to those who are loyal to God (cf. v. 35). See Pss 5:11; 119:132; Isa 56:6.

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This Psalm uses the two most common names for God.

- Elohim (i.e., a title that focuses on Deity as creator, sustainer, and provider of
all life of this planet) ‒ Ps. 69:1,6,13,29,30,32,35 (also a variant form in
Ps. 69:3, "God" [Eloah] and Ps. 69:6, "God" [Eloah]
of Israel")

- YHWH (i.e., a title that focuses on Deity as savior, redeemer, covenant-making God)

- Lord of hosts, Ps. 69:6

- YHWH, Ps. 69:13,16,31,33

SPECIAL
TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C., D.

SPECIAL
TOPIC: Lord of Hosts

- The psalmist feels estranged from life, family, and friends (cf. Ps. 69:8) because of his
trust in God (cf. Ps. 69:9). Jesus uses this Psalm to describe His own feelings of rejection
by fellow Jews. The difference is, the psalmist wants revenge and judgment (cf. Ps. 69:22-28),
but Jesus asks for His persecutors' forgiveness based on their ignorance (cf. Luke 23:34).

- The Jewish Study Bible, p. 1356, thinks the historical setting of this psalm is a prayer for the
return of Abraham's seed to Canaan and the temple (cf. vv. 9-12; 33b).

- This Psalm has many prayers, some expressed as IMPERATIVES and some
as IMPERFECTS used in a JUSSIVE sense (see note at Ps. 69:6).
